gap: The dots sit loose under the words. In A the gap from baseline to the top of the dots is ~13 px, against ~12 px in B, while the letters rise ~3 px higher in the row (top of the tall letters at y≈3 vs y≈6). That leaves the dots about 1 px further from their word, so the mark looks lower on the page. A's letter advance is also wider, 26.0 px against 25.6, so the same two lines run 26 px longer (1664 vs 1638 px) and the text sets a little looser.
gapTheirs: B's dots have a softer edge: the crop holds ~224 px of #F1ACA6 and ~256 px of #ED7D74 around the 6 px #ED766B cores, where A's dots are cleaner with rounded corners (edge columns 4-6-6-6-6-4). At reading distance B's dots look very slightly blurry next to A's. The glyphs also look a touch heavier (~7675 px of #191919 against ~7073, though B's crop is 26 px narrower).
verdict: The two are almost the same: a row of 6 px coral dots every 8 px, the same #ED766B, the same seven-mark pattern, and DRAFFT left unmarked in both. B puts its dots right under the word and sets the line tighter, so each mark clearly belongs to the word above it. A's dots are pushed about a pixel lower and its line runs 26 px longer, which a close reader feels as looseness, not something wrong. Neither mark shouts, but B's feels more like it belongs to the text.

states.name: on-dark
states.gap: The dots on the first row sit at sub-pixel offsets. A 1-px scan through the 'definately' mark shows split column pairs (24/29, 32/37, 40/45…) before it settles onto a clean 8 px grid, so the row reads a little soft and uneven. B's dots sit exactly every 8 px (18, 26, 34…). A's dot rows are also blurrier, with pixel counts per row of 128/181/189/188/179/126 against B's 64/160/192/192/128/64. The monospace advance is wider too, about 26.0 px against 25.6, which makes each line about 26 px longer (1664 vs 1638) and every word slightly more spread out.
states.gapTheirs: B's marks are thinner on the second row. The 'Teh'/'comittee' dot rows fade out more at top and bottom (38/97/116/116/77/38 px against A's 73/110/110/110/110/73), so the second-row dots look slightly smaller and lighter than the first-row dots. In A the dot rows below both lines look the same weight.
states.verdict: You would struggle to tell these apart: both use the same #cf807e dotted mark, 6 px dots on an 8 px period, about 14 px under the baseline. Both leave DRAFFT unmarked and mark the same four words. B wins on small details. Its dots sit on whole pixels and its tighter 25.6 px advance keeps the line compact, while A's first-row dots look faintly smeared and its text is set a bit looser. Most writers wouldn't notice without zooming in, but a typographer at 400% would pick B.
secondary: Image sizes differ: A 1664x135, B 1638x135. The heights match; the widths differ because the character advance differs.
Mark colour is the same in both, with #CF807E as the main dot colour.
Dot rows fall at the same heights in both (y 47–52 and 121–126), so the gap under the baseline matches within about 1 px.
Both mark 'definately', 'recieved', 'comittee' and 'Teh', and both leave the all-caps 'DRAFFT' unmarked.
Each dot run is about as long as its word in both, starting about 2 px left of the first letter.

states.name: focus-light
states.gap: A is wider for the same two rows: 1664 px against 1638 px, +26 px or +1.6%, from a looser monospace advance of about 26.0 against 25.6 px per cell. So each mark starts later: the first dot of 'definately' sits at x=364 in A and x=358 in B. The dots are also a touch softer. Both have 58 dots on the first mark row, but A's middle rows fill 334 px against B's 348 px, which means some of A's dots land between pixels and lose part of their 6 px core to anti-aliasing.
states.gapTheirs: B has a stray blue blob (#36BFFA, about 5 px wide) at its bottom-left edge, x≈47–52, y≈131–132. It looks like the top of a caret or caret handle from the row below showing through the bottom of the frame. A writer reads that as noise. Apart from that, B has nothing A lacks: same dots, same colours, same greying, same unmarked word.
states.verdict: You can't tell these two apart at reading distance. Both put a row of round, coral dots under each misspelling, on an 8 px period, 6 px across, sitting on the same rows (y=47–52 and 121–126), and neither dims the dots when the words around them go grey. A's text runs 1.6% wider and its dots are a little softer, so the marks look slightly less crisp under the pale words. B gets the nod for tighter spacing and cleaner dots, even with that stray blue fragment at its edge.

states.name: focus-dark
states.gap: The dots are hard-edged 6 px blocks with almost no anti-aliasing (about 60 partial-tone pixels at the dot rows, against about 1,400 in B), so at 1x they look like a row of square beads, not round dots. The glyphs are also 3 px taller (ink starts at row 3 against B's row 6, sharing a baseline near row 43), so the dim-grey #707070 prose sits heavier on the same 1a1a1a ground.
states.gapTheirs: A blue (#2AA0E0-ish) blob about 5×3 px pokes into the frame at x48–52, y132–134, under 'the', with nothing above it to explain it. Its dots also carry a ring of #7F5352/#C27A78 half-tone edge pixels (658 + 752 px), which blurs the 6 px dot on its 8 px period into a soft pinkish smear.
states.verdict: The two are almost the same frame. Both dot rows sit at exactly y47–52 and y121–126 in the same #cf807e with the same 8 px period, the same seven words and 'Teh' are marked, DRAFFT is left alone, and the out-of-focus prose holds #707070 while the marks keep their ink. B's frame has a stray blue fragment at the bottom-left edge that a writer's eye would snag on every time they glanced down. A's crisper, slightly blockier dots are the smaller fault. Neither one gets the dots right: A's are too square and B's are fuzzy.

states.name: syntax-light
states.gap: The type is thinner and lighter. At 400% the stems of 'definately' and 'Teh' are visibly lighter and softer than B's, and the cell advance is 26.0 against 25.6 px, so the same two rows run 26 px wider (1664 vs 1638 px). Under Syntax highlight A leaves the misspelled 'comittee' and 'Teh' in body black while 'definately' and 'recieved' get Category colours, so the marked words don't read as one set.
states.gapTheirs: B's dots are softer at the rim. Measured across 400 px of row 1, the dot rows fill 64/127/190/190/127/64 px from top to bottom, against A's 23/128/155/156/128/13. A's dot edges cut off more sharply. Ink (#ED766B), 6 px diameter, 8 px period and depth under the baseline (y47–52 and y121–125) are identical in both.
states.verdict: The spell mark itself is a draw: the same salmon round dots, 6 px across on an 8 px period, at the same depth under the baseline, marking the same four words and leaving DRAFFT alone. The difference is the prose sitting above the dots. B's heavier, denser monospace holds the line and makes the dots read as a note under the word. A's lighter strokes let the dots compete with the letters. A also leaves two of the four marked words uncoloured under Syntax highlight, which looks like a bug rather than a choice.

states.name: syntax-dark
states.gap: Under Syntax highlight, two of A's four marked words lose their Category colour: 'comittee' and 'Teh' are plain near-white (~#d0d0d0), while B colours them the same orange (~#d4876a) as 'notes' and 'noon'. DRAFFT is also neutral in A but gold (~#b8964e) in B, and 'before' is green in A but neutral in B, so the colouring disagrees on 4 words across 2 rows. The dots are nearly identical: 8 px period, peak #CF807E, about 6 px across.
states.gapTheirs: B's first row sits 2 px lower (glyph tops at y=15 against 13) while its dot row stays at y≈47, so the gap from baseline to dots is about 1–2 px tighter than A's (~10 px against ~11 px). The dots under 'Teh' and 'definately' start about 1 px further right of the glyph's left edge. The line is also 26 px narrower (1638 against 1664) because B's cell advance is 25.6 against A's 26.0.
states.verdict: The dots are close enough to call a draw: same period, same ink, same size, and neither app dims them. What decides it is the syntax layer under the dots. In A, a misspelled word can drop out of its Category and go white, so a typo looks like a different part of speech from its neighbours. B keeps each misspelled word in its Category colour and lets the dots do the flagging, which is how a writer checking grammar and spelling in one pass wants it.

A's band runs 57–130 around letter tops at 80 and a baseline at 109, which is 23 above and 21 below. B's highlight hangs about 5 px low. B's dots also start 13 px under the baseline against A's 12, so the dots sit a little further from the word.
states.gapTheirs: Dots are softer at the edges. Across the first dot row, 128 px are the paler #ED7D74 and 32 px are #F1ACA6, around 384 px of #ED766B. In B the same row is solid #ED766B with only about 14 px of fringe, so A's dots look slightly smudged at 1x.
states.verdict: The dots are the same in both: same size (6 px), same colour (#ED766B), same rows (47–52 and 121–126). Both skip DRAFFT, and both keep the dots under the selected 'recieved'. What separates them is placement. A's selection wraps its letters evenly, while B's highlight sags below the line, like a text box that was never lined up. A's blurrier dot edges are the smaller flaw; the misplaced highlight is what you'd notice every time you select a word.

states.name: select-dark
states.gap: The dots start 13 px under the baseline against A's 12 (baseline row ~34 against 35, with both dot rows at y 47–52). Its bigger glyphs sit in the same 74 px pitch, so the lines feel tighter. The selection band starts at y=60 against A's 57, which leaves an extra 3 px of dark gap between the two selected rows, so 'recieved' and 'the notes' look like two separate blocks rather than one selection.
states.gapTheirs: Its type is about 6% smaller than B's in the same 74 px line pitch: cap height is ~30 px against 32 (x-height ~21 against 22 rows) and the image is 1638 px wide against 1664. Next to B the prose reads a touch small and grey, and the rows of misspelling dots under 'definately' and 'comittee' look a little more prominent against the smaller glyphs.
states.verdict: You would have to lay these on a lightbox to tell them apart. The dots have the same 8 px period and are ~4 px round in both, the ink is #C27A78 against #C67B79, and the dots stay at full strength under the selection in both. B makes the glyphs bigger without giving the lines more room, and its dots drift a pixel away from the word, so the mark feels slightly less attached to it. A is a touch airier and the dots stay tight to the word; that's the only reason it wins.
